references_experience.text: Tout manquement sera sanctionné. Les produits échantillonnés devront être présentés tels qu’ils seront livrés en cours d’exécution du marché. Les étiquettes de chaque échantillon devront être conformes aux exigences du présent marché. Au cas où il existerait un désaccord entre les spécifications annoncées et celles relevées sur les échantillons, c'est toujours la formule la plus avantageuse pour le client qui sera retenue pour devenir base contractuelle du marché. Les cartons de livraison porteront obligatoirement le nom du candidat avec la mention « ECHANTILLONS MARCHE CROUS ». Il sera accompagné d’un bon de livraison détaillé précisant la référence et/ou la marque de chaque produit, ainsi que les fiches techniques de l’ensemble des échantillons. Le défaut de présentation des documents exigés (étiquettes, bon de livraison, fiches techniques) entraînera également le rejet de l’offre. Il est rappelé que les échantillons demandés, ainsi que les précisions apportées dans l'offre par les fiches techniques, constitueront la définition contractuelle des produits retenus. Tous les échantillons remis par les candidats, retenus ou non, restent acquis à l’établissement. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

certifications_partner.text: o facilitate this, the Department provides an in-house “Fixture Script” library which provides a pattern. Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. Keeping Tests Green Whenever a project starts the Department will ensure that the initial CI pipeline for their project branch (of the Trunk) is green. Thereafter it is the responsibility of the project to keep the pipeline “green”. The Department uses a number of approaches to achieve this. Other supporting systems that make up the technology landscape include Facial Imaging Matching System (FIMS), and the General Registers Office (GRO) system. The BOMi’s scope will continue to grow in both size and complexity to (a) support the Department’s expanding Digital requirements, (b) consolidate its technology stack, and (c) continue to support new or changing legislation as it arises. The current technology platform is .NET Framework 4.x deployed to Windows Servers. In due course these will be upgraded to .NET 6 (aka .NET Core) at which time the Department will plan to deploy these systems, either for testing and/or production, on Linux/Docker when appropriate. The Senior Technical Development Advisor (TDA Lot 1) has acted as an independent strategic technical advisor across the IS Division, providing guidance on a range of SDLC and architecture related concerns. The TDA (Lot 1) helped product and platform teams deliver secure, resilient, and high-quality solutions more rapidly through the adoption of modern engineering practices and automation technologies. The TDA (Lot 1) role focused on shaping governance process and technical direction and procurement activities, translating complex technical issues into clear recommendations and implementation plans. Key areas of contribution included Continuous Integration, Release and Deployment, SDLC platform engineering, application security process and governance, Test Data Management modernisation, Developer Experience, contract testing, and SDLC platform architecture, particularly for the Department’s BOMi Platform. The TDA (Lot 1) also played a significant role in defining product and platform ownership models, associated team charters and enhanced IT governance approaches. In addition, the role supported various technical procurements through technical assessments.

ip_data_security.text: teostamaks Lepingus nimetatud tegevusi, võttes sealjuures arvesse teenuse iseloomust tulenevat andmesubjektide isikuandmete töötlemist. Lisa eesmärk Lisa eesmärk on kokku leppida volitatud töötleja õigustes ja kohustuses isikuandmete töötlemisel, millest pooled juhinduvad lepingu täitmisel (edaspidi teenused). Lisa jõustub pärast selle allkirjastamist mõlema poole poolt. Lisa rakendatakse, kui volitatud töötleja töötleb vastutava töötleja nimel vastavalt lepingule kliendi isikuandmeid. Lisa kujutab endast isikuandmete töötlemist puudutavat andmetöötluse lepingut vastavalt Euroopa Liidu isikuandmete kaitse üldmäärusele (EL 2016/679) (edaspidi GDPR). Andmesubjektide kategooriad ja isikuandmete liigid, mida teenuse osutamisel töödeldakse, isikuandmete töötlemise kestus, iseloom ja eesmärgid ning vastutava töötleja poolt antud juhised on leitavad lepingus ja selle lisades. Pooled kohustuvad järgima isikuandmete kaitse üldmäärust (EL) 2016/679 ja kohalduvaid Eesti õigusakte ning vajadusel viima sisse parandusi käesolevasse lisasse, et toimida kooskõlas eelmainitud regulatsioonidega. Vastuolude korral lepingu ja lisa sätete vahel tuleb juhinduda lisa sätetest. Mõisted Lähtuvalt lisa eesmärgist ja kooskõlas GDPR-iga on kasutusel järgmised mõisted: „tehnilised ja organisatsioonilised meetm

The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. forms_signatures.text: ment of the Army (HQDA) G-4 Logistics Initiatives Group is the directorate responsible for leading the Army’s digital transformation in logistics and Installation, Energy, and Environment (IE&E). The G-4 drives policy, governance, investment strategy, and the technical integration of logistics automated information management systems. Their strategic focus centers on logistics modernization through integrated information systems, scaling artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) analytics, and improving supply chain reliability across Army operations. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate iss

l, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommen

tive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical compositions represented in the Army accession and training population. • Accessibility (Section 508): Must provide an accessible alternative process for Soldiers and Cadets who are unable to use, or elect not to use, the scanning solution; any user-facing digital interface must strictly comply with Section 508 accessibility standards. • Data Ownership & Licensing: Must allow the Government to retain exclusive ownership of all Soldier and Cadet sizing data as well as any vendor-generated technical or derived data. • Hardware Agility & Openness: The proposed solution must be hardware- agnostic to the greatest extent possible, avoiding dependency on proprietary, single-source capture devices. The software application must be capable of evolving to support new generations of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) devices. The physical hardware proposed for the pilot must be agile, deployable, and suitable for the respective operating environments

When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

ointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor licensed to do business in Portugal who provides services to other local RFP 19GE5026Q0035 – LES Health Insurance Services for U.S. Embassy Lisbon Page 6 of 21 organizations as well as to the U.S. Mission; employees working on an intermittent or When Actually Employed (WAE) schedule; Peace Corps personal services contractors and Recreation Association employees. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively
